servesNote: 5 portions — Sunday, five people, one cook, and the last shared meal before everyone leaves. ⭐ This is not a hard dish, it is a hard piece of scheduling, and the card is written accordingly.
adaptations: ⭐ THE WHOLE PLAN TURNS ON ONE FACT: a single oven cannot be at 200°C and 90°C at the same time, so the box that cooks the food cannot hold it until the food has finished cooking. Every decision below is arranged around that.

⚠️ CHECK THIS BEFORE SUNDAY, BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE PLAN: is your grill a separate compartment, or the element inside the main oven? Separate — the toast happens at the very end and arrives hot (the T-4 step). Inside the oven — you cannot grill and hold at 90°C in the same box, so the toast runs through the toaster early and is racked (the T-25 step). Follow one route and skip the other; both are on the timeline.
⏰ THE TIMES ARE COUNTED BACK FROM SERVING. T-50 means fifty minutes before you want to eat. The sausages set the clock and everything else fits around their thirty minutes.

prep: ⏰ THE NIGHT BEFORE — DO NOT SKIP THIS. You will have been up early, and every one of these takes two minutes cold and feels impossible at 8 am.
Wipe and halve the mushrooms — brush them clean, ⛔ never wash them, you would only be adding water you then have to drive back off.

Halve the tomatoes across the equator and cut out the green eye. Salt the cut faces and leave them cut-side down on kitchen paper in the fridge, which draws the free water out overnight instead of onto the plate.
Slice the black pudding 1.5–2 cm thick and skin it. Separate the bacon rashers onto a plate. Open the beans into the saucepan.
Stack the plates by the oven, lay the table, and put the butter out to soften.

steps.text: T-50 · Oven on, 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Everything out of the fridge, the eggs especially — cold eggs spread thin and cook unevenly.

T-40 · Sausages onto the LOWER tray, lightly oiled, well spaced. ⛔ Do not prick them. Pricking lets the juices out and dries the meat — a myth that survives on repetition. The sausages set the clock for the whole morning.

T-30 · Turn the sausages. Second tray onto the UPPER shelf: mushrooms oiled, in a single layer with real gaps between them, unsalted; tomatoes cut-side UP in the remaining third, with a folded strip of foil dammed between the two. ⭐ The gaps and the dam are the whole trick. Moist food cannot brown until the surface water has gone, so a crowded tray steams and you get grey weeping mushrooms — and tomato liquid running into the mushrooms ruins both.

T-25 · TOASTER ROUTE ONLY. Toast, five batches, through to T-13. Stand each slice upright in a rack as it comes out and ⛔ do not butter it yet. Laid flat it traps its own steam and goes limp; buttered hot it goes soggy. Cool and crisp is the correct outcome, and it is what a toast rack is for. ⚠️ Skip this step entirely if your grill is a separate compartment.

T-20 · Black pudding onto the sausage tray. It is already cooked — this is reheating and crisping only. Beans on the lowest ring, lid on, with a knob of butter floating on top. The lid and the butter both stop the skin forming; the film is just evaporation from a still surface.

T-18 · Bacon on the hob — six rashers, 3–4 minutes a side. Snip the fatty edge so it does not curl. ⚠️ If water pools in the pan, pour it off — back bacon is wet-cured loin and will poach itself in its own liquid rather than browning. ⭐ It is on the hob and not in the oven on purpose: back bacon is lean loin, it holds worse than anything else on the plate, and this frees the oven shelf you do not have while leaving a pan of rendered fat for the eggs.
T-14 · Second batch of bacon. Salt the mushrooms NOW — not earlier. Salt draws water out, which is exactly what you spent the last fifteen minutes driving off.

⭐⭐ T-12 · Crack all ten eggs into four small bowls and season them. This is the single most important step on the card and it is the one people skip. You cannot crack ten eggs one at a time into hot pans — the first is three minutes older than the last and they will not finish together. Cracked ahead, each pan fills in one pour.

T-10 · EVERYTHING OUT. Open the door wide for a minute and dial the oven down to 90°C. Sausages, black pudding and bacon onto a warmed platter lined with kitchen paper and into the oven — sausages and pudding loosely covered, bacon UNCOVERED. Covering the bacon traps steam and undoes the crisp you just made. Plates in. Mushrooms drained — they keep weeping — into their own dish, in. ⛔ Tomatoes stay OUT, on their own tray, touching nothing.
T-9 · Two large frying pans on medium, bacon fat plus a little butter.
T-5 · Eggs in — one pour per pan, five each. Cover. Two minutes on the heat.
T-4 · GRILL ROUTE ONLY: ten slices of toast in two batches, while the eggs sit. ⚠️ Watch it — the seeds on multiseed scorch before the crumb browns. Skip if you toasted at T-25.

⛔ T-3 · Pans OFF the heat, lids on, and leave them alone. Three minutes gives soft-set yolks, four gives medium. Do not lift the lids. The residual heat finishes them with no attention from you, which is the entire point — it hands you back the three minutes when you most need your hands.
T-2 · Butter the toast. Stir the beans, heat off.
T-1 · Plates out. Load everything except the eggs — beans, sausages, bacon, black pudding, mushrooms, and tomatoes last, at the edge of the plate, away from the toast.
